title: Edge SDK fanout pattern and offline coda quickstart
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview:

This quickstart documents a lightweight, production-oriented pattern for client SDKs that must: (1) fan out requests across multiple Redwood endpoints (hosted, dedicated, private), (2) operate with intermittent network connectivity (offline coda behavior), and (3) emit consistent telemetry for cost and latency attribution. It combines an SDK architecture, concrete code + CLI examples, recommended defaults, and a triage checklist for the top support issues we see in field integrations.

Goals:
- Provide a resilience-first SDK pattern that preserves developer ergonomics.
- Keep per-token cost signals and latency attribution intact across offline/edge flows.
- Standardize fallback/circuit behavior so downstream services can reason about degraded modes.

Who should use this doc:
- SDK authors (internal) building client-side libraries for Redwood.
- Integrations engineers embedding Redwood into mobile/embedded/web apps.
- Support engineers troubleshooting edge/offline customer issues.

High-level architecture:
1) Client runtime (edge SDK): local process or browser worker that exposes Redwood client API. Responsible for request shaping, local cache, and telemetry aggregation.
2) Router/fanout layer: deterministic policy-based router inside SDK that selects endpoints in this order: local-private (if configured) -> Dedicated (pinned tenant) -> Hosted. Router uses named policies (latency-first, cost-first, hybrid).
3) Offline coda queue: persistent write-ahead queue (IndexedDB on web, SQLite on mobile, local file on desktop) with delivery worker and backoff/circuit state machine.
4) Telemetry aggregator: batched usage + timing events emitted to telemetry pipeline; includes markers for "offline-delivery", "replay", and "fallback-to-hosted".

Key concepts (definitions):
- Offline coda: the SDK state after a network interruption where new requests are queued locally and older requests may be replayed once connectivity returns.
- Fanout policy: deterministic selection logic that decides whether a request is sent to private/dedicated/hosted endpoints or is queued. Policies are expressed as short strings (e.g., "latency:v1", "cost:low-v2").
- Delivery token: a lightweight UUID attached to each outgoing request to enable per-request tracing across local queue -> router -> Redwood runtime.

Recommended defaults (rationale included):
- Queue storage: use IndexedDB (web) or SQLite (mobile) by default with a soft limit of 50MB. Rationale: allows large prompt bundles and ensures persistence across app restarts.
- Max queued requests: 500 (configurable). Prevents runaway disk usage on low-storage devices.
- Default fanout policy: latency-first for interactive SDKs, cost-first for batch/analytics SDKs.
- Replay window: 72 hours default; older queue items expire and emit a "dropped-offline" event.
- Circuit threshold: mark endpoint unhealthy after 6 consecutive 5xx or timeout (2s) failures within 10s window.

Quickstart: add the Edge SDK to an app (JavaScript example)

1) Install (npm):

$ npm install @redwood/inference-edge-sdk@latest

2) Minimal initialization:

const { EdgeClient } = require('@redwood/inference-edge-sdk');
const client = new EdgeClient({
  apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY,
  endpoints: { private: 'https://private.example.internal', dedicated: 'https://dedicated.redwood.ai', hosted: 'https://api.redwood.ai' },
  fanoutPolicy: 'latency:v1',
  storage: 'indexeddb', // web default
  telemetrySampling: 0.5 // 50% span sampling on low-resource devices
});

3) Send a request with offline-safe options:

const response = await client.generate({
  model: 'redwood-v1-7b',
  prompt: 'Summarize user session for support',
  offline: { allowQueue: true, priority: 'user-visible' },
  timeoutMs: 4500
});

If device is offline, SDK returns a queued acknowledgement: { status: 'queued', deliveryToken: '...' } and later emits a replay event with final delivery status.

API example: envelope format sent to Redwood runtime (canonical JSON)

{
  "delivery_token": "uuid-1234-...",
  "policy": "latency:v1",
  "source": "edge-sdk-js@1.2.0",
  "client_time": "2026-01-11T17:03:00Z",
  "payload": { "model": "redwood-v1-7b", "input": "..." },
  "meta": { "offline_coda": "true|false", "replay_count": 0 }
}

Configuration table (recommended settings):

| key | default | notes |
|-----|---------|-------|
| storage | indexeddb/sqlite | Platform-specific persistent store |
| maxQueuedItems | 500 | Items older than replayWindow are dropped |
| replayWindowHours | 72 | Configurable per-app policy |
| circuitFailures | 6 | Failures in 10s window before marking endpoint down |
| endpointTimeoutMs | 2000 | Per-endpoint socket/response timeout |
| telemetryBatchMs | 5000 | How often telemetry is batched and sent |

(If rendering table is not supported in client, use the JSON snippet below for programmatic defaults.)

Programmatic defaults (JSON):

{"storage":"indexeddb","maxQueuedItems":500,"replayWindowHours":72,"circuitFailures":6,"endpointTimeoutMs":2000,"telemetryBatchMs":5000}

Operational runbook (steps for support)

1) Reproduce locally
  a. Use "edge-sdk dev-mode" which simulates offline scenarios and allows forcing endpoint failures.
  b. Confirm whether problems are in: queue persistence, router policy, or delivery worker.
2) Triage logs and telemetry
  a. Look for events: offline-queued, replay-attempt, replay-success, replay-failure, dropped-offline.
  b. Correlate delivery_token with inbound request on the runtime side. Use the Delivery Log lookup tool (internal) with the token.
3) Resolve common symptoms
  - Symptom: SDK returns "queued" but no delivery on reconnect. Check: storage integrity (corrupted DB), queue processing worker crash, or missing network permissions.
  - Symptom: Excessive replays causing duplicate charges. Check: replay_count not incrementing, missing idempotency header. Fix: ensure client sends X-Redwood-Delivery-Id and runtime honors idempotency.
  - Symptom: High latency after reconnect. Check: batch flush size and telemetryBatchMs causing spikes; tune telemetryBatchMs and enforce jitter.

Top support issues & canonical fixes (examples)

1) Issue: Duplicated completions after offline replay
Fix: Ensure SDK sets "X-Redwood-Delivery-Id: <delivery_token>" and runtime returns 202 with { accepted: true, idempotent: true } when a delivery token is recognized. If duplicates already occurred, issue a reconciliatory compensation flow (customer-visible).

2) Issue: Queue growth on low-storage devices
Fix: Enforce maxQueuedItems and implement LRU eviction with a policy to keep high-priority items. Surface a storage-exhausted event to the host app and offer a compact mode (compress prompt payloads).

3) Issue: Telemetry attribution mismatch (edge vs hosted)
Fix: Add explicit span tags: source=edge-sdk, fanout_policy, offline_coda=true/false, delivery_token. Ensure ingestion pipeline joins on delivery_token to attribute cost/latency properly.

Testing & QA guidance

- Unit tests: mock IndexedDB/SQLite, fake time to validate replayWindow expiry, assert circuit open/close transitions.
- Integration tests: run against local Redwood dev runtime with knobs for 5xx injection and latency.
- Performance tests: ensure median enqueue latency < 3ms on nominal devices and batch drain time scales linearly with queue size.

Docs-site operating checklist (for docs maintainers)

1) Page canonicalization: mark this page as the canonical quickstart for "edge/offline" SDK patterns using the docs-site metadata tag: canonical=true.
2) Snippets: keep examples in /docs-site/snippets/edge-sdk so they are included in automated snippet tests.
3) Release notes: when the SDK default fanoutPolicy or replayWindow changes, add a compatibility note in the SDK changelog and the consumer-facing migration guide.

Rollout plan for breaking changes (example: change replayWindow default)
1) Feature flag the new default behind an opt-in config in SDK vX.Y.
2) Release SDK with telemetry that reports the value used per-install.
3) After 30 days of opt-in telemetry validation, flip default in minor release and communicate via changelog + in-console migration notice.

Appendix A — CLI debug commands

# Start the dev-mode simulator (forces offline every 15s)
$ rwd-edge dev-mode --simulate-offline 15s

# Inspect local queue (prints JSON)
$ rwd-edge queue inspect --limit 50

# Force replay of all queued items (use with caution)
$ rwd-edge queue replay --confirm

Appendix B — Telemetry sample event (line-delimited JSON)

{
  "event":"replay-attempt",
  "delivery_token":"uuid-1234",
  "policy":"latency:v1",
  "queued_at":"2026-01-11T17:02:00Z",
  "replayed_at":"2026-01-11T17:05:02Z",
  "outcome":"success",
  "endpoint":"dedicated"
}
